ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an energized solenoid, and a dashed horizontal axis points horizontally from the solenoid to the single-turn circular ring on the right; the circular ring is located beside the right end of the solenoid. The solenoid current is labeled I, the arrow on the right lead points upward, and the arrow on the left lead points downward; the direction of the desired induced current i is marked on the circular ring. Reasoning: According to the right-hand grip rule, from the winding direction of the solenoid current I in the figure, it can be judged that the magnetic flux produced by the solenoid at the right circular ring passes through the circular ring along its axis. Then according to the right-hand rule, looking at the loop current i shown in the figure, the magnetic field direction it produces in the circular ring is the same as the direction of the original magnetic field of the solenoid, that is, it is enhancing the original magnetic flux. According to Lenz's law, if the induced magnetic field is to enhance the original magnetic flux, it indicates that the original solenoid magnetic flux must be decreasing. To make the solenoid magnetic flux passing through the circular ring decrease, the distance between the solenoid and the circular ring should be increased. Therefore the solenoid should move away relative to the circular ring.

method.method_draft: First inspect the picture: identify the solenoid axis running horizontally toward the loop, the direction of current I in the solenoid, and the shown direction of current i in the loop. Use the right-hand grip rule on the solenoid current to determine the direction of the solenoid's magnetic flux through the loop. Then use the right-hand rule on the indicated loop current i; this current produces a magnetic field through the loop in the same direction as the solenoid's field there. Since the induced field is trying to reinforce the original solenoid flux, Lenz's law implies the original flux must be decreasing. The way to decrease the solenoid's flux through the loop is to increase their separation, so the solenoid must be moved away from the loop.

method.method_draft: Inspect the diagram and assign magnetic poles. Use the right-hand rule on the solenoid winding to identify the pole at the solenoid end facing the loop. Use the same loop-face rule on the indicated current i to identify the pole on the loop face facing the solenoid. The visual current directions make the facing pole of the loop opposite to the facing pole of the solenoid, so the induced interaction would be attractive. An induced attraction opposes the motion only when the solenoid is being pulled away from the loop; if the solenoid were approaching, Lenz's law would require a repulsive induced face instead. Therefore the solenoid should be moved away from the loop.

图像描述：图中左侧是一个水平放置的通电螺线管，虚线表示其轴线；右侧同轴放着一个圆形线圈。螺线管上标有电流 I，在靠近右端的引线处箭头向上；圆环上标有感应电流 i，箭头位于圆环左上侧，表示图示方向的环流。

推理：按右手定则判断螺线管绕线电流方向，螺线管靠近圆环的右端为北极。再对圆环使用同样的电流环面规则：从螺线管一侧看，图示的感应电流 i 使圆环面对螺线管的一面成为南极。因此，螺线管面对圆环的一端与圆环面对螺线管的一面是异名磁极，会相互吸引。根据楞次定律，感应电流产生的磁作用总是反抗相对运动或磁通变化；若要产生这种吸引作用，它应当反抗两者分离的运动。因此螺线管必须相对圆环被移远，而不是移近。
